1029. **The basis document (provisional decision P457).**
      - _What it held._ `StoredBasis.documents`
        (`runtime/runner/src/compiled/basis.ts`) named every document the piece
        made that is no row, and a run that made one wrote the path
        `documents/<doc>` of the document of the basis, which the storage and
        every holder store whole. In FabriChat at 100 messages (`SCALE_BASIS`, a
        new option of the harness) the list held 3,462 documents: 2,081 entities
        of streams, 737 places of the scope `user`, 325 of the scope `session`,
        103 created cells, 103 element records, 103 outputs of the scope `user`
        and a few others; at 500, 16,662, of which 10,081 streams.
      - _First form, taken back: leave out what a resume derives again._ A piece
        that has documents of a scope resumes whole (note 892), so the entities
        of streams and the documents of a scope were left out of the list. Of
        the documents listed in the corpus's whole resumes (`--resume`, counted
        before and after the list's sync), 1,679 were reached by the links the
        resume follows from the result anyway, 167 were brought by the list
        alone (104 entities of streams, 44 documents of the space, 19 of the
        scope `user`) and 130 by neither (70 of the scope `session`). The corpus
        showed both left-out kinds are needed: a whole resume that wrote the
        marker of a stream it had not brought was refused with a stale confirmed
        read at sequence 0 (`showcase/wordsearch/play.tsx`, whose streams the
        stored result reaches only through a scope instance), and so was one
        that wrote a place of the scope `user` it had not brought
        (`examples/group-chat-lobby/group-chat-lobby.tsx`,
        `showcase/scrabble/scrabble.tsx`).
      - _Decision, P457: the list is spread over part documents._ Every document
        the piece made that is no row is listed, as before, in one of 256 parts
        by `basisPartOf`, the hash the numbers of the sources are spread by
        (`basisMadePartDocumentOf`); the document of the basis names the parts
        that exist (`made`). A run that made a document writes its path in its
        part, and a part that has no document yet is written whole.
        `storedBasisOf` reads the parts, `syncBasis` brings them for every
        resume, and a part the document names and the storage does not hold is
        no basis, as for the numbers. A refused commit that wrote the basis has
        the next record write every part whole, as it writes the numbers. Chosen
        over a document per row (the list grouped by the element key that made
        each document) because the hash parts exist for the numbers and are the
        same mechanism; the cost is that a part holds about one in 256 of the
        documents, so what a send writes grows with the room at a 256th of the
        rate.
      - _Tests._ `runtime/runner/test/compiled/basis-documents.test.ts` over
        `fixtures/scoped-rows-made.tsx` (a `map` over an array of references
        whose rows each have a stream and a place of the scope `session`, and an
        event that adds an item in a document the piece makes): before, the
        documents of the basis that an item added after 100 others writes listed
        270 documents more than after 10 (the document of the basis whole, three
        documents for each item); after, they list 6 and 3, the parts that name
        what the item made; a runtime that resumes the piece from its basis
        shows every row; no refusal. `resume.test.ts`: a derivation behind an
        added item writes one document more, the part of the list that names the
        item.

1030. **`Instance.rootOf` without the read of `failed` (step 3): built in a
      scratch worktree, not landed.**
      - _What was built._ `rootOf` gives a cone that reads the result of an
        operation the reference to its outcome, `state.key(OUTCOME)`, and reads
        nothing of the state document, which is of the scope of the operation.
        The member `failed` is gone. The error state of a request that was not
        made (SS §6.2, step 1) is then read where the reference is read through:
        `#requestTransactions` writes it as the outcome itself, in place of the
        record of `pending`, `result` and `error`, and clears `requestHash`, so
        the next request that holds no error state is made and the outcome is a
        record again; and `Store.locate` gives the error state for a path below
        a position that holds one, as a read of a member of a value in an error
        state gives it (PL §5.2), so a reader through the reference takes the
        error state and a reader that passes the reference on reads nothing. A
        client that reads the stored link reads the error state too, where with
        `failed` it read a record with `pending` false. The patch is
        `r22-send-growth/step3/rootof-experiment.patch`.
      - _What it gave._ Over `fixtures/scoped-wish-view.tsx` (a tree that places
        `profile.result` of a `wish` of the scope `user` as an attribute bound
        to a cell, beside the rows of a `map` over an array of references), with
        two principals, the scope instances hold 3,014 bytes at 10 items and
        25,334 at 100 before, the tree being of the scope `user`, and the same
        at both sizes after. `exec/test/` passed with it; the one case of
        `compare/test/` that failed in that run was of the first form of P457
        (note 1029).
      - _Why it was not landed._ `examples/profile-group-chat/main.tsx` on the
        runner path, with or without a resume: the whole result becomes the
        error state "a computation of the scope `user` stored what it derived in
        a document of the space (output)". The read of `failed` had made the
        result's cone of the scope `user` from its first evaluation, since the
        cone binds the handler `sendMessage` with the wish's result as
        `profile`. Without it the cone is of the space until the first message
        stores that result as its `authorProfile` (a link of the scope `user`,
        note 1016); then `participants`, a `computed` over the messages, reads
        through the link and is of the scope `user`, and the assembly over its
        result stores its rows by `Instance.#generated` in a document of the
        space (the name `#scopeOfOutput` gave before the value was found to be
        of a scope) in the evaluation of the result's cone, which
        `#refuseStoredForEveryKey` then refuses. So the defect is the executor's
        handling of a value that becomes of a scope after it was stored whole in
        a document of its own: the stored document has to move to the scope
        instance with the value, as the place of a value does (`#staleAside`
        when a place moves to a narrower scope), and the write to the document
        of the space is no derived write of the entry that evaluates the
        assembly. That is a change of its own with its own test; it was not
        built, and step 3 waits on it.
      - _Where the error state is read, in the form built:_ in the outcome, by
        whatever reads through the reference to it: a cone that reads a member
        of the result (`fetched.pending` takes the error state, as
        `exec/test/effects.test.ts` "is not requested where the cone of its
        request failed" asserts), a handler body that reads it through a handle,
        and a client that reads the stored link.

1031. **What keeps the room's rendered tree of a scope (step 4).** Traced in a
      scratch worktree with `rootOf` as in note 1030 and `Handle.resolveAsCell`
      following the links at the handle's position (the experiment of note 1022;
      how handles follow links is excluded from this round and nothing of it is
      built): each evaluation of the room's tree cone (value 586 of
      `FabriChatRoom`) recorded the first read of each scope instance it made
      and the stack of the read (`ScopeInstances.resolve`). Four reads, in the
      order they were found:
      1. _The read of `failed` in `rootOf`_ (note 1030).
      2. _The spread `...view` in the result of the room's inner pattern_
         (`room.tsx`, `return { ..., [VIEWS]: { room: view }, ...view, ... }`).
         `view` is a record the body builds, whose members are values of other
         cones (`messageRights`, `canSend`, `viewer` and others of the scope
         `session`). The crate emits a spread whose argument is no value of
         another cone as `...$h.v(...)`, which reads the record whole and
         follows each reference to the place of a scoped value; the room's tree
         forces the inner instance's result (`$h.at(room, [UI])`), so the tree's
         cone reads every scoped member. With the spread of a record the body
         builds emitted as a pass (`Want::Pass`: the members, references
         included, are placed as they are, as a spread copies them in
         JavaScript), the tree went from the scope `session` to the scope
         `user`. No planning apart is needed: the members are already values of
         their own; the tree only has to stop reading them. A change of
         `structure` in `src/emit.rs`, with fixtures emitted again.
      3. _`{profileWish[UI]}`_ (`room.tsx`, the `div` of the profile setup): a
         path of the result of a `wish` of the scope `user`, placed as a child
         of JSX. The slot (`$h.slot(585, [$h.pick(13, UI)])`) observes the
         value, so `Host.slot` reads it whole through the operation's state
         document. Passed on by reference instead (tried by returning the
         reference from `Host.slot` for a slot whose root is an operation of a
         scope narrower than the space), the tree is of the space. As a rule
         this is P451's for an operator expression, extended to a path of a
         scoped place written as a child or an attribute value: the crate plans
         it as a value of its own, or binds the slot as `identity` where the
         position only passes it on. It needs planning apart or an `identity`
         slot, decided by the crate; a change of `hoisted_scope` and
         `place_scope` in `src/plan.rs`.
      4. _The links of the scope `user` the rows reach through `authorProfile`_
         (note 1016): with `resolveAsCell` returning the handle, as on this
         branch, the rows of the main conversation read the wish's state through
         each message's `authorProfile`, and their cones are of the scope
         `user`. This is the work on how handles follow links.
      - _Measured in the scratch worktree, a send at 10 messages,_
        `SCALE_STAND_INS=table`, one run each, the documents a send changes:
        with 1 and 4 changed (note 1022's experiment), the tree is of the scope
        `session`, its session instance holds 206 KB, and the send changes 258

        instance of the scoped outputs still holds 185 KB, 243 KB; with 1, 2, 3

        instance holds it, 98 KB; with 1, 2 and 3 and `resolveAsCell` as on the
        branch, the tree is of the space and the rows' cones of the scope
        `user`, with a user instance of 17.7 KB, 108 KB; with 1 and 2 alone, 121
        KB with a session instance of 42 KB. On the branch at its head, 105 to
        112 KB, with the session instance of the tree at 35 KB. At 10 messages
        the variants differ little in bytes; what changes is where the rows of
        the main conversation are stored. In a scope instance a scoped tree
        holds them whole, which grows with the room (190 KB at 100 messages,

### CFC questions deferred, round twenty-two

Noted and not resolved, by the owner's instruction of 2026-11-22.

1. Notes 1027 and 1028: the marker of a stream that a derivation makes for the
   row of an element whose value carries a confidentiality clause is written
   under no record, takes the join of the derivation, and is measured against
   the empty ceiling of a document no schema declares a policy on, so it is
   refused at every derivation while the element exists. Which label the marker
   owes is FabriChat round two's question 4 (note 745). New here: the join is of
   what the derivation evaluated, not of what the values it stores came from, so
   whether the marker is refused depends on what a retry evaluates again; at
   `5db1c2658d` a retry that evaluated nothing carrying the clause stored the
   marker with no label.
2. P457: a part of the list of the documents a piece made is written under no
   record, as the document of the basis was, and takes the join of the
   derivation that writes it last; it names documents that several derivations
   made, under several joins. The same held for the document of the basis, which
   named them all.
3. Note 1030, not landed: with the error state of a request that was not made
   held in the outcome, the outcome carries the label the request transaction's
   join gives it, as the member `failed` did, and a reader that reads through
   the reference consumes it where a cone that only passes the reference on
   consumes nothing.
4. Note 1031, planned: a spread of a record a body builds, emitted as a pass,
   places each member at its position with the label of that member's value,
   where the read of the whole record joined the labels of every member into
   each position the spread gives. A change that stores less label, to be ruled
   on before it is built.

## Round twenty-three: the room's tree of the space, and the rows of a filter

Round twenty-three (2026-11-24), on the branch
`claude/compiled-pattern-scoped-rows` from `4df0c33bdf`. The notes are numbered
from 1035, the provisional decisions from P458. The logs are in the folder
`r23-tree-scope/` of the session. Whenever a note says `map` or `filter`, it
names the case. Times are on an Apple M5 Max with 18 cores at the load averages
given, from other sessions; the counts do not depend on the load.

1035. **Findings, first.**
      - _Soundness, fixed: a value of one user was written into a document of
        the space._ The document that holds what a body returned whole for an
        output (`Instance.#generated`) is named by the scope its value was found
        to have when it is first stored. A value that becomes of a scope later,
        as a `computed` over an array of references does when an element starts
        to hold a link into a scoped document, is stored in a document of that
        scope from then on, but the document of the space named before kept its
        source: a read that reached it through a link stored elsewhere evaluated
        the value for the acting key and stored it there, where every reader
        reads it. On the runner path such a write, made inside a derivation, is
        what `#refuseStoredForEveryKey` refused in
        `examples/profile-group-chat/main.tsx` (note 1030). Fixed with three
        defects found beside it (note 1036).
      - _Soundness, fixed: a principal's rows read `null`._ The rows of a `map`
        over the result of such a `computed` (an array of plain values generated
        from scratch) stood in the result document of the space after the value
        became of a scope, keyed by one principal's values, and a row of a key
        that stayed held its reference into the document of the space; and once
        both principals had evaluated the rows, the place of the scoped rows of
        one principal was never brought up to date again, since nothing marked
        it through an assembly formed again for another key (note 1036).
      - _Soundness, fixed: a `filter` over the result of a `map` stored
        `{ at: [] }` in place of an appended row._ The branch of
        `Instance.#reassemble` that brings a `filter` up to date pushed the
        source of each element as the value of the result; for the rows of a
        `map`, the source is the record that names the row's entry, not the row
        (note 1039).
      - _Scale, fixed: the room's rendered tree is of the space._ With the read
        of `failed` gone from `Instance.rootOf` (note 1037) and
        `profileWish[UI]` read as a path (note 1038), the tree is in the result
        document of the space, and no scope instance holds the rows of the main
        conversation; each row of the main conversation is a row document of the
        scope `user` of its own (note 1040; note 1031 has the rows read the
        wish's state through `authorProfile`, read 4). Note 1031 had the spread
        `...view` keep the tree of the scope `session` as well; with the other
        two reads gone it does not: it keeps the room's result of that scope,
        and the tree is an output of its own. A send at 1,000 messages changes
        714 to 729 KB where it changed 2.37 MB (note 1040).
      - _Scale, open, found in this round's measurements: the store step of the
        room's result follows the room._ With the tree in the result document,
        `Instance.#storeResult` places the result again at each send and notes
        again the record of each position of the tree whose inputs changed at
        every position those inputs reach (`#noteRecord`): 29 ms per send at 100
        messages, 404 ms at 1,000, where the step took 90 ms at 1,000 before.
        The piece's phases together still take less than before (1,160 against
        1,212 ms per send at 1,000), since the storage phases fell with the
        bytes, but the seed at 1,000 takes 694 s against 530 s. Not fixed; plan
        in note 1042.
      - _Scale, fixed: a `filter` brought up to date looked at every element._
        An append to a source of 1,000 elements looked at 2,504 elements; it now
        looks at 4, at every size, for a `filter` over an array of references,
        over an array of plain values in place, and over the result of another
        `filter` (note 1039).
      - _Scale, open: an edit that takes an element in the middle out of a
        `filter`, or puts one in, numbers again every member behind it_ (750 at
        1,000 elements), as a `sortBy` and a `flatMap` do and as the element
        table of the construct over the result does for its own elements. Plan
        in note 1042.
      - _Scale, open: a `filter` over the result of a `map` is formed whole at
        every change_, since its elements are rows and not references (the
        branch now forms it whole where it stored the wrong value). Plan in
        note 1042.
      - _Scale, open: the three lists of links of the room's tree are written
        whole at each send at 100 messages_ (16 KB each): the tree is of the
        space now, and its collections are stored as lists in documents (P392,
        P393), whole up to 128 rows. Figures in note 1040.

1036. **A value that becomes of a scope after it was stored in a document of the
      space (step 1; provisional decision P458).**
      - _The reproduction._ `fixtures/scoped-generated.tsx`: a `computed` over
        `items`, an array of references, whose block body is not promoted,
        returns for each item its owner, a link that a handler stores into an
        item, to the acting user's nickname, a state cell of the scope `user`;
        the rendered tree holds a `map` over the result, whose rows pass each
        element on; a row's handler keeps the reference to its element in a
        state cell of the space. `fixtures/scoped-generated-count.tsx` adds a
        read of the array's length to the tree, so the tree becomes of the scope
        too, as `participantCount` does in `profile-group-chat`. On the executor
        in memory the defect does not take the form of the refusal, since the
        write to the document of the space comes from a read that follows a link
        outside the derivation's transaction (`result()`); on the runner path it
        is the refusal (note 1030).
      - _Four defects and what was built._ (1) The source of the document of the
        space, `Store.sources`, stores what the value is for the acting key; it
        now stores nothing where the value is of a narrower scope than the
        document (`#generated`, `named() === id`), so a document of the space
        holds what every reader may read, the value it held while it was of the
        space. (2) A row of a key that stayed passed the reference to its
        element on and read nothing a change marks, so it kept the reference
        into the old document; an element whose place moved with its key
        unchanged now marks what is kept under its key as not current
        (`samePlace`, `#placeMoved` in `assembled`). (3) The unit of the
        assembly stood in the result document of the space with the rows of one
        key, and `#scopedRows` is consulted only when a unit is placed; a unit
        whose assembly is found to be of a scope key is placed again, as
        `#formOf` places such an assembly from the first (`#storeUnit`). (4) An
        assembly is formed again for each key and not set aside, so a place of
        the scoped rows of one key, set aside while another key acted, was
        reached by no mark when its key's value changed; dropping the assembly
        of a key now marks its users of that key, set aside or not
        (`#markScopedUsers` in `#forActing`).
      - _P458._ A document that holds what a body returned whole for an output,
        named in the space while its value was of the space, is no place of the
        value once the value is found to be of a scope: nothing stores the value
        there again, the rows that hold references into it are evaluated again,
        and a unit of an assembly over it moves to the scope instances. The
        document is left in the store with what it held. As for the place of a
        value (`#valuePlace`), the move is one way, since the scope of an entry
        only narrows.
      - _Tests_ (`exec/test/scoped-view.test.ts`, two principals): over both
        fixtures at 10 and 100 items, each principal reads the rows its own
        nickname selects (`Ann` for one, the empty name for the other), no
        document of the space holds `Ann`, and no document links to the document
        of the space but the state cell the handler wrote; over both at 10
        items, each principal reads its own nickname after both changed it. At
        `4df0c33bdf` the document of the space held the acting user's nickname
        (four cases), and over `scoped-generated.tsx` a row read `null` after
        the nicknames changed. Each of the four parts was taken out once:
        without (1) the document of the space holds `Ann`; without (2) the rows
        link to it; without (3) a principal's row reads `null`; without (4) a
        row reads `null` after the nicknames changed. Without both (1) and (2),
        `profile-group-chat` on the runner path with the patch of note 1037
        gives the refusal again; with either, the module is handled.

1037. **`Instance.rootOf` without the read of `failed` (step 2; provisional
      decision P459).**
      - _Landed as note 1030 built it,_ without its debug output: the result of
        an operation is the reference to its outcome, the error state of a
        request that was not made is the outcome itself, and `Store.locate`
        gives that error state for a path below it.
      - _Where the error state is read now_ (`fixtures/failed-request.tsx`, an
        effect whose request holds a value whose cone fails for one address): a
        cone that reads a member of the result takes it; a cone that passes the
        reference on reads nothing, is not evaluated again when the request
        fails, and holds the link; a handler that reads the result through a
        handle takes it, where at `4df0c33bdf` it read nothing of it; a client
        that reads the stored link reads it in the outcome, and reads a record
        again once a request is made. Tests in `exec/test/effects.test.ts`; the
        second and third were seen failing at the head of step 1 (the cone that
        passes the reference was evaluated again, and the handler stored nothing
        of the error state). The test over `fixtures/scoped-wish-view.tsx` of
        note 1030 is kept: the scope instances held 3,014 bytes at 10 items and
        25,334 at 100 before, the same at both sizes after.
      - _P459._ Where a request is not made because it holds an error state (SS
        §6.2, step 1), `outcome` holds that error state in place of the record
        of `pending`, `result` and `error`, and no request is outstanding;
        `execution-and-storage.md` §6.4 says so now.
      - _`profile-group-chat`._ With step 1, the module on the runner path and

1038. **`{profileWish[UI]}` (step 3; provisional decision P460).**
      - _Why the slot observed the value._ The crate planned `profile[UI]` as a
        pick by a key computed at run time (`$h.slot(n, [$h.pick(m, UI)])`, a
        slot that observes the `shape` at `*` and a pick slot that observes the
        `value`), so the cone of the tree read the result of the `wish`.
        `language-subset.md` §4.3 has an element access by a well-known key of
        the API static, as one by a literal is; the crate did that for a key of
        a record literal and for the checker, and not for a member read.
      - _What was built._ `Emitter::well_known_key` in `src/plan.rs`: a computed
        key of a member read that is a well-known key of the API (`UI`, `NAME`
        and the others `api::ApiValue::WellKnownKey` lists) names the segment a
        record literal gives the same key, `$UI`. The child then passes its
        place on by the rule that already applies to a state cell or a path with
        a string key (`Emitter::pass`, an `identity` slot), and the tree holds a
        link of the scope `user` to the outcome's `$UI`.
      - _P460: bound as `identity`, not planned apart._ The child is a path, not
        an operator expression, and reads nothing; today's runtime passes a path
        placed as a child by reference and gives a child a node of its own only
        where it is a computation. P451's rule is for an expression that reads
        the value; a position that passes a place on reads it in neither path.
        So P451 is not extended; the crate follows §4.3. A pick by a key the
        module computes (`profile[key]`) stays a pick that reads the container.
      - _Tests._ `tests/plan.rs`,
        `a_member_read_by_a_well_known_key_is_a_static_path`: the child gives an
        `identity` slot at `$UI` and the tree one pick, that of `profile[key]`;
        seen failing without the change. `exec/test/scoped-view.test.ts` over
        `fixtures/scoped-wish-child.tsx`, two principals at 10 and 100 items:
        the tree stays in the result document of the space, no scope instance
        holds it, and an edit of one item writes the same two documents at both
        sizes; before, the scope instances held 2,772 and 25,092 bytes. No other
        emitted fixture changes.

1039. **The rows of a `filter` (step 4; provisional decision P461).**
      - _What it visited per element._ At each splice of the source or changed
        flag, the branch for `moved` or `flagged` of `#reassemble` formed the
        members from every element of the source, one object each, pushed each
        element's source as the value, and compared the members it held with the
        new ones from both ends; and a pass that changed no member counted as a
        change (a new version and a delta with no splice), so the unit of a
        stored result compared all its keys. Counted with
        `Counts.elementsVisited` (new: the elements `#reassemble` looks at one
        by one, and the rows `#storeUnit` compares by key; the probes of a
        binary search are not counted).
      - _What was built._ The positions of the source that a splice put in or
        whose flag changed are looked at: the members before the first and
        behind the last are found by binary search over the members by where
        their elements stand now (both are monotonic: a member before the first
        touched position kept its position, and one behind the last of them kept
        its order from the end), and the members in between are spliced, as one
        splice of the result. A pass that changes no member is none: the version
        of the assembly stays, so a construct over the result, brought up to
        date from the delta of each version, does not fall behind and form
        itself whole at the next change; and `#storeUnit` leaves the stored rows
        of an assembly whose members, value and version are those it saw. An
        element that is no reference forms the assembly whole, as it does for a
        window, which fixes the value a `filter` over the result of a `map`
        stored.
      - _P461._ As above. The same code covers a `filter` over an array of
        references, over an array of plain values in place, and over the result
        of another per-element construct whose elements are references, as a
        `filter` over the result of a `filter`; over the rows of a `map` it is
        formed whole.
      - _Counts_ (elements looked at, at 10, 100 and 1,000 elements of
        `fixtures/filter-rows.tsx`: `shown`, a `filter` over `items`, and
        `titled`, a `filter` over its result; before / after):

        | change                                  | references                 | plain values in place       |
        | --------------------------------------- | -------------------------- | --------------------------- |
        | an append the predicate keeps           | 29, 254, 2,504 / 4, 4, 4   | 29, 254, 2,504 / 4, 4, 4    |
        | an append the predicate leaves out      | 22, 202, 2,002 / 2, 2, 2   | 22, 202, 2,002 / 2, 2, 2    |
        | an edit that keeps the membership       | 0, 0, 0 / 0, 0, 0          | 25, 250, 2,500 / 6, 6, 6    |
        | an edit that takes the last element out | 22, 247, 2,497 / 3, 3, 3   | 23, 248, 2,498 / 4, 4, 4    |
        | an edit that takes the middle one out   | 0, 271, 2,746 / 0, 75, 750 | 21, 272, 2,747 / 2, 76, 751 |
        | a removal of the last element           | 19, 199, 1,999 / 0, 0, 0   | 19, 199, 1,999 / 0, 0, 0    |

        An edit of a plain value in place changes its key (no key field is
        declared), so it is a splice of the source. No assembly is formed whole
        in any of them, before or after.
      - _Tests_ (`exec/test/growth.test.ts`): each change above but the middle
        one, and an append left out followed by one kept, looks at as many
        elements at 10 as at 100 and forms no assembly whole, over references
        and over plain values in place; 12 of the 13 cases failed at the head of
        step 3 (an edit that keeps the membership over references looked at
        nothing before either). Without the version that stays, the append left
        out followed by one kept formed the `filter` over the result whole. Over
        `fixtures/filter-of-map.tsx` the result holds the rows each change
        keeps; at the head of step 3 an appended row read as nothing.

1042. **Planned, not built.**
      - _The position of a member of an assembly._ A member of the result of a
        `filter`, a `sortBy` or a `flatMap` carries its position in the result
        (`Element.index`), and each splice that puts in another number of
        members than it takes out gives every member behind it a new object with
        its new position: 750 members at 1,000 elements for an edit in the
        middle of a `filter`. No reader of the members of an assembly reads that
        position: `#table` numbers the members of an upstream again, and
        `#reassemble`, `#storeUnit` and `#segment` read the members by their
        place in the array. The plan is to keep no position in the members an
        assembly holds, which changes the type the element table shares with
        them, so it is a change of representation across every per-element
        construct and is not built here. The element table of the construct over
        the result keeps its positions, since a cone that reads the index of its
        element depends on them, and its splice numbers again every element
        behind it as well; bounding that needs positions that a splice does not
        rewrite, an order-statistics structure, which is a decision of its own.
      - _A `filter` over the rows of a `map`._ Its elements are the rows, values
        the result holds as they are, and each kept row is a dependency of the
        assembly (`given` in `assembled`) beyond the dependencies on the
        predicate's entries, which `#reassemble` does not know, so a change of a
        row forms it whole. The plan: `Rows` records the entry of each kept row
        with its key, and `#reassemble` puts a changed row's new value at the
        member's place, as it puts an entered member in; with that, an element
        that is no reference need not form the assembly whole. No decision is
        needed; not built, for time.
      - _The rows of the main conversation are of the scope `user`,_ each a row
        document of that scope of about 12 KB at 100 messages, through the reads
        of the rows that follow `authorProfile` (note 1031, read 4): the work on
        how handles follow links, excluded from this round.
      - _The lists of links of the room's tree,_ three lists of 103 links
        written whole at each send at 100 messages: below 128 rows a list is one
        document (P393), so each send writes it whole. Figures at 1,000 in
        note 1040.
      - _The store step of a result that holds the tree_ (note 1040): the result
        entry of the room is evaluated again at each send and placed again
        whole, and each position whose record's inputs changed has its record
        noted again at every position its inputs reach, which for the positions
        of the tree that depend on the messages follows the room (29 ms at 100
        messages, 404 ms at 1,000). Note 923 has `Instance.#noteRecord` as an
        open cost; with the tree of the space it is the largest phase of the
        executor in a send. The plan is note 923's: register a record by the
        inputs it names and not by every position they reach, so that noting it
        again costs what changed. Not built.

## Round twenty-four: the store step of a result, and a filter over rows

Round twenty-four (2026-11-24), on the branch
`claude/compiled-pattern-scoped-rows` from `71fefaf1e3`. The notes are numbered
from 1044, the provisional decisions from P462. The logs are in the folder
`r24-store-step/` of the session. Whenever a note says `map` or `filter`, it
names the case. Times are on an Apple M5 Max with 18 cores at the load averages
given, from other sessions; the counts do not depend on the load.

1044. **Findings, first.**
      - _Scale, fixed: the store step of the room's result placed the whole
        result again at each send._ It formed and compared 621 positions, the
        rendered tree included, where the tree and most members were the very
        values placed before. A record or an array that is the value placed at
        its position before is now neither formed nor compared (P462): 83
        positions at every size. The positions did not follow the room; the
        noting of records did (next item).
      - _Scale, fixed in part: each record given again was registered at every
        position its inputs reach._ Fourteen records of the result name the
        inputs of `facts`, about four positions per message held, and each was
        removed from and added to the index of label readers at every send:
        6,800 to 6,900 positions at 100 messages, 29,200 to 29,300 at 500.
        Records whose inputs hold equal content now share one set of positions,
        changed where the positions differ (P463): 1,012 to 1,028 at 100, 4,212
        to 4,228 at 500, 8,212 to 8,228 at 1,000. `#storeResult` takes 90 ms per
        send at 1,000 messages where it took 319 ms (both without the harness's
        walk), and the piece's own time per send is 323 to 337 ms where it was
        549 to 565 ms, at the same load (note 1050).
      - _Scale, open: what a send still registers grows with the room._ The row
        of each new message has two places, in its row document of the scope
        `user`, whose records name the inputs of `facts` through two outputs;
        they are records of a new key, so each send registers their set whole
        (about 8 positions per message held). And every row's records keep the
        positions of the inputs of `facts` as they were when the row was made,
        since a row is not given its record again when `facts` changes: the
        index of label readers holds, over the life of the room, a set per row
        as large as the room was then, which grows with the square of the room.
        This is older than this round (each record kept its own array of
        positions). Plan in note 1052; it needs a decision on what a record that
        names another output is a reader of.
      - _Structure, a defect of this round found by the measurement and fixed:_
        with `SAME` counted as `KEPT` is, an array that holds another value at
        every position was compared position by position where a member held a
        record placed before: the window of the newest messages was written as
        112 positions per send at 100 messages, where it was written whole as
        one (note 1045, test over `fixtures/shared-window.tsx`).
      - _Performance, found and fixed:_ with the sets shared, the question
        whether a record's positions consume another label after a change
        (`#readsChangedLabel`) copied the shared set for each record (140 ms per
        send at 1,000 against 46 ms before); it is answered once per set.
      - _Scale, fixed: a `filter` over the rows of a `map` was formed whole at
        each change of a row or of its membership._ It is brought up to date by
        row (P464): 3 elements looked at for an append at 10, 100 and 1,000
        elements, over the result of a `map` over an array of references and
        over an array of plain values in place, where the assembly was formed
        whole.
      - _Scale, open: the records below a member that is the value placed before
        are each asked about (`#sameRecords`),_ which computes the inputs of
        each output found there and their number: the work follows the outputs
        the member holds, not what changed (11 ms per send at 1,000 in the
        room). Plan in note 1052.
      - _Scale, open: a middle edit of a `filter`, a `sortBy` or a `flatMap`
        numbers again every member behind it_ (250 at 1,000 elements of a
        `filter` over the result of a `map`), and the element table of a
        construct over the result does the same; step 5 is planned and not
        built, as it is not contained (note 1049).
      - _Harness: `Instance.streams()` is called once per binding_ (note 1048);
        the 353 ms per send of round twenty-three at 1,000 messages were the
        harness's.
      - _Recorded, not changed:_ the stream markers of the result are made again
        at each evaluation of the result entry, so a record that holds one is
        never the value placed before, and its link is compared at each send;
        and `facts`, an authored body, reads about eight positions per message
        held at each send (8,061 reads at 1,000).
1045. **Placing a result again (step 1; provisional decision P462).**
      - _What was visited._ `Instance.#storeResult` places the value of the
        result entry whenever the entry is another one (`#place`): `#formOf`
        forms the whole value, the rendered tree included, and `put` compares
        each position with what it holds, giving at each position left as it was
        the record of the output nearest above it (`#unchangedOutput`, which
        finds that output by a scan of every recorded output). The result entry
        of the room is evaluated again at each send because it holds
        `messages.count` and the other facts, while most of its value is the
        value of cones that were not evaluated again: the tree, the records of
        `about`, `participants` and the others. A send placed 621 positions at
        100, 500 and 1,000 messages (`Counts.positionsPlaced`, new). The number
        does not follow the room; what followed the room in the store step was
        the noting of records (note 1046).
      - _What was built._ `#place` takes the value placed at the place before
        (the value of `#storedResult` for the result, the row's value for a row
        of a unit), and a record or an array of the new value that is the one
        the previous value held at its position is given as `SAME` (`stored`,
        `#storedMember`): nothing below it is formed or compared. A unit below
        such a member stands where it stood and is due; the records its
        positions would have given are given as those of places left as they
        were (`#sameRecords`): the record of the output nearest at or above the
        member, and that of each output below it that holds a value, found
        through a tree of the recorded paths (`#recordedTrie`, `#trieAt`),
        expanding `*` over what the place holds and stopping at the path of a
        unit or of an index stored by itself. Each record is asked about once
        per comparison (`#checkedNow`): nothing is evaluated while a place is
        compared, so its inputs are the same at every position it covers. The
        link record of a stream is compared whole, as a link is (a stream that
        stays is given no record, which `put` said and did not do for a stream's
        members). A result document that an aborted transaction wrote is placed
        whole again (`#abort` clears `#storedResult`).
      - _A defect found by the measurement and fixed._ `differsThroughout`
        counts a member that holds `KEPT` as one that does not differ; with
        `SAME` counted the same way, the window of the newest messages, whose
        entries each hold the author's profile record placed before, was
        compared and written position by position: 112 writes per send at 100
        messages where there was one. `SAME` is filled from what the position
        holds before the comparison (`withSame`); `holdsKept` is about `KEPT`
        alone.
      - _P462._ As above. Today's runtime writes a result by diffing the whole
        value against what is stored (`diffAndUpdate`); here what is compared is
        what is not the value placed before, so the work follows the cones
        evaluated again. The records of the outputs below a member that is the
        same are still asked about, one by one: the work for them follows the
        outputs the member holds, not what changed (note 1052).
      - _Tests_ (`exec/test/store-step.test.ts`, over
        `fixtures/result-tree.tsx`: a result whose tree holds the rows of a
        `map` over an array of references, each item a document of its own,
        beside the count and the titles a body forms from every item through the
        handle of the array): an append places at most 8 positions, the same at
        10 and 100 items (51 before); an append gives the records of what it
        changed and of nothing else, and a rename the record of the titles alone
        (passing before and after); over `fixtures/shared-window.tsx` the window
        is written whole (three writes of a title before the fix of
        `differsThroughout`). In `exec/test/transaction-hooks.test.ts`, over
        `fixtures/unchanged-record.tsx` (a record whose named output read
        another position and gave the value it gave), the record of the place is
        given again; without `#sameRecords` it is not. In
        `compare/test/store-step-labels.test.ts`, the labels stored at the
        count, the titles, the heading of the tree, the list and the rows of
        `result-tree.tsx`, each item under a clause of its own, after an append
        and after a rename: the same at `71fefaf1e3` and after.

1046. **Registering a record (step 2; provisional decision P463).**
      - _What it cost._ `Instance.#noteRecord` kept, for each record key, the
        positions its inputs reach, and at each noting removed the key from
        every position it was registered at and registered it again at every
        position the new inputs reach, through the index of label readers
        (`#recordReaders`, a tree of documents and path segments). In FabriChat
        fourteen records of the room's result (`messages/count`, `oldestAt`,
        `newestAt`, `threads`, `legacyReplies` at the top level and in
        `$VIEWS/room/messages`, and four positions of the tree and of a row's
        place) name the inputs of `facts`, which read about four positions per
        message held; each of them registered 417 positions at 100 messages. A
        send registered 6,798 to 6,910 positions at 100 and 29,198 to 29,310 at
        500 (`Counts.recordRegistrations`, new: the positions at which a reader
        was added or removed).
      - _What was built._ Records whose inputs hold equal content share one set
        of positions (`ReadSet`): its name is the instance and the number
        `InputsDigests` gives the inputs with their element keys, or the
        positions of the record's own element where it names the inputs of
        another element (`#ownReads`). The set is registered once in
        `#recordReaders`, and it keeps the folds over a collection and the
        tables of member groups its inputs read (`#recordFolds` and
        `MemberGroups.records` name sets). Noting a record names the content of
        its inputs and nothing more (`#pendingReads`); the sets are brought up
        to date when the transaction ends, when a label change asks for them, or
        when the positions of one record are asked for (`#flushReads`): the
        records that take one new content share a set; a set all of whose
        records take the same new content is changed where the positions, the
        folds and the tables differ (`#retarget`); any other new content gets a
        set of its own, and a set no record names any more is dropped.
        `#recordsReading`, the rows a body wrote (`#labelsRead`) and
        `#relabelCreated` read the sets, and `labelsChanged` asks once per set
        whether its positions consume another label (`#readsChangedLabel`),
        which it asked once per record, over a copy of the record's positions.
      - _What it does not change._ What a record says: the records given, their
        inputs and the table are the same; which records a label change alone
        reaches is the same (test below), and the labels stored are the same
        (the test of note 1045). What noting a new content still costs: the walk
        of its inputs to list their positions (`#readsOf`), once per new content
        and not once per record, and the number `InputsDigests` gives each
        record's inputs, formed from their whole text.
      - _P463._ As above. Today's runtime forms a label from the read set at
        each commit and keeps no index of the records that read a label; the
        index exists here so that a label change alone forms again the labels of
        exactly the records that read it (`plan-and-label-templates.md` §4.1),
        and it now costs what changed in the content of the inputs.
      - _Tests_ (`exec/test/store-step.test.ts`): an append to
        `fixtures/result-tree.tsx` registers as many positions at 10 items as at
        100 (133 and 1,213 before, 4 and 4 after); after an append, a label
        change alone at a position the body read before the append, at one it
        read for the appended item, and in a document nothing reads, reaches the
        same records before and after (the count, the titles and the row's child
        of the item; nothing).

1047. **A `filter` over the rows of a `map` (step 3; provisional decision
      P464).**
      - _Why it was formed whole._ The assembly of a `filter` whose elements are
        the rows of another per-element construct holds each kept row's value
        and depends on the row's entry (`given` in `assembled`); the branch of
        `#reassemble` for a `filter` knew the dependencies of the elements'
        predicates and not those, so a change of a kept row was a suspect it
        could not place and formed the assembly whole, and an entered element
        that is no reference formed it whole as well (P461).
      - _What was built._ The formation records the entry of each kept row with
        its key (`Rows.kept`), the dependencies on those entries standing behind
        those of the elements, in the order of the members. `#reassemble` puts
        an entered member that is a row with the row's value and a dependency on
        its entry (`#rowDependency`, the same dependency `Host.depend` gives for
        a path), splices those dependencies with the members, and puts a changed
        row's value at its member's place, found by binary search, reported as a
        row of the delta (`delta.rows`, as a `map` reports one), which
        `#storeUnit` places.
      - _P464._ As above; the same code covers a `filter` over the result of a
        `map` over an array of references and over an array of plain values in
        place, and over the result of any per-element construct whose members
        are rows held whole (`isRowSource`: a source at no path below the row).
        A member that is a row at a path below it forms the assembly whole, as
        before.
      - _Counts_ (elements looked at, assemblies formed whole, evaluations, at
        10, 100 and 1,000 elements of `fixtures/filter-of-map.tsx`; before /
        after, the same over an array of references and an array of plain values
        in place but where marked):

        | change                                  | before                     | after                        |
        | --------------------------------------- | -------------------------- | ---------------------------- |
        | an append the predicate keeps           | 8, 53, 503; formed whole   | 3, 3, 3                      |
        | an append the predicate leaves out      | 3, 3, 3                    | 3, 3, 3                      |
        | an edit that keeps the membership       | 5, 50, 500; formed whole   | 0 (references), 4 (in place) |
        | an edit that takes the last element out | 4–5, 49–50, 499–500; whole | 2 (references), 4 (in place) |
        | an edit that takes the middle one out   | 0–3, 49–50, 499–500; whole | 0–3, 26–28, 251–253          |
        | a removal of the last element           | 0, 0, 0                    | 0, 0, 0                      |

        The evaluations are the same before and after (2 to 4). "Formed whole"
        counts the elements the store step compared by key (`#storeUnit`), not
        those the formation read. An edit in the middle still numbers again
        every member behind it (note 1049).
      - _Tests_ (`exec/test/growth.test.ts`): each change of the table but the
        middle one, and an append left out followed by one kept, looks at as
        many elements at 10 as at 100 and forms no assembly whole, for a
        `filter` over the result of a `map` over an array of references and over
        an array of plain values in place; eight of the twelve cases failed
        before (formed whole). The case that holds the rows each change keeps
        passes before and after.

1048. **The harness (step 4).** `compare/fabrichat/scale.ts` found the entity of
      the stream it sends to with `Instance.streams()` at each send, which walks
      the stored result and follows every link in it; it finds it once per
      binding now (`entityOf`), and prints the load average with each timed
      send. Nothing else changes. The before at 1,000 messages was run with the
      same change (note 1050).

1049. **The members of an assembly without positions (step 5): planned, not
      built.**
      - _What renumbers._ A member of an assembly is an `Element` and carries
        `index`; the branches of `#reassemble` for a `filter`, a `sortBy` and a
        `flatMap` give every member behind a splice that puts in another number
        than it takes out a new object with its new position
        (`rowsNow[index] = { ...rowsNow[index], index }`), a window makes new
        members, and the formation numbers them (`numbered` in `assembled`). The
        readers of the members read them by their place in the array:
        `#storeUnit` reads `members[index].key`, `#reassemble` finds a member's
        element through `byKey` (`placeOf`), and `#table` of a construct over
        the result numbers the members again for its own element table
        (`upstream.members.map((member, index) => ...)`).
      - _The plan._ A type `Member` (`Element` without `index`) for
        `Entry.members`, `Rows.members` and `assembledElements`; `numbered` gone
        from `assembled`; the renumbering loops gone from the three branches and
        the window's members made without positions; `#table` numbering the
        members it takes as elements, as it does now. Tests first in
        `exec/test/growth.test.ts`: an edit that takes the middle element out of
        `filter-rows.tsx` and of `filter-of-map.tsx`, and one that moves a key
        in `sort-by.tsx`, looks at as many members at 10 as at 100.
      - _Why it is not built._ It is not contained: removing the positions of
        members bounds the assembly's own work, but a construct over its result
        keeps an element table whose positions a cone that reads the index of
        its element depends on, and `#reassemble` numbers again every element of
        that table behind a splice (the loop from `low` to the end where
        `high < 0`), so a middle edit of a `filter` with a `map` over its result
        still visits every element behind it. Bounding that needs positions that
        a splice does not rewrite, an order-statistics structure for element
        tables, which is a decision of its own (note 1042).

1052. **Planned, not built.**
      - _A record that names another output, registered by that output._ The
        sets of positions of P463 are snapshots of content: a row whose places
        name `facts` keeps the positions `facts` read when the row was made, and

        template names (a set per cone instance, brought up to date when that
        cone instance is evaluated, with the records that name it as readers)
        would cost what changed at each evaluation and hold one set per cone
        instance. It changes which records a label change alone reaches: a row's

        given, and not by one it no longer reads, which is what the label of the
        row's place, formed from the template that names `facts`, would take if

        per plan. Not built: the positions an element's binding names

        evaluation, which the closure has to cover.

        that holds one can be the value placed before. Not built.
      - _The members of an assembly without positions_ (note 1049).

### CFC questions deferred, round twenty-four

Noted and not resolved, by the owner's instruction of 2026-11-22.

1. P462, the link record of a stream compared whole: a position that holds a
   stream's link no longer asks for the record of the output nearest above it.
   Before, the comparison went into the members of the link record and asked for
   that record at each of them, so it was given again where the output's inputs
   had changed; now it is given again only where another position below that
   output asks for it. A change that can leave a label formed from earlier
   inputs where an output covers nothing but links of streams; in FabriChat the
   records given per send are the same (300).
2. P462, `#sameRecords`: for a record or an array that is the one placed before,
   the record of the output nearest at or above it and of every output below it
   is asked for, where the comparison of each position asked only for the
   outputs nearest to some position compared. A record whose output covers no
   position that no deeper output covers, or one reached through both a literal
   and a `*` segment, can now be given again where its inputs changed and it was
   not given before: its label is formed from the current inputs. The labels
   stored in the test of note 1045 are the same before and after.
3. P463: the tables of member groups a set of positions reads are those that
   exist when the set is brought up to date (`#flushReads`), not those that
   existed when the record was noted; a table made between the two is read, so a
   label change there reaches the record. No rule of a label changes.
4. P464: no rule of a label changes; a changed row of a `filter` over the rows
   of a `map` is placed with the record of the result at its position, as the
   rows the assembly formed whole were.
5. Note 1052, planned: a record whose template names another output keeps, as
   the positions a label change alone reaches it through, those the named
   output's inputs read when the record was given; the record is not given again
   when the named output's inputs change and its own value does not. A reader by
   the named output's cone instance would be reached by what the named output
   reads now. Which of the two a record owes is the question; the second would
   form again labels the first leaves as they were.

## Round nineteen, fourth continuation: writes and reads through a cell another document holds

The owner's questions of 2026-11-24: whether a compiled `.set()` is right for a
cell whose position holds a write redirect; what a write through a state cell a
pattern returns does, where today's runtime stores the cell as a write redirect;
that a write rule that follows every link is wrong, as the chain of
`runtime/runner/test/schema-links.test.ts` shows; and what a handler stores with
`kept.set({ current: selected.get() })` and `selected.resolveAsCell()` when
`selected` holds a link to the item chosen now. The owner then proposed that a
read follow exactly one link past the write redirects and point at what it
reached, so that each read of a cell of cells gives one level. Notes from 1060,
the provisional decisions P470 and P471. The test is
`runtime/runner/test/compiled/cell-writes.test.ts` over the fixture
`compare/fixtures/cell-writes.tsx`: `Writer`'s handlers write cells that are
inputs and store what an input is into another cell, `Selector` holds the item
its handlers choose in a state cell, `Reader` returns a read of its input from
value code, and `Owner` returns two state cells it makes. Each pattern runs on
today's path, compiled from the same source, or as a compiled piece.

1060. **Findings, first.**
      - _Soundness of writes, fixed: a write of a value followed every link._
        Today's runtime follows the write redirects at the position and replaces
        the first plain link it reaches. Over
        `start => redir => first -> second -> data` (`=>` a write redirect, `->`
        a plain link) a compiled handler's `chain.set(v)` wrote `data`; today's
        replaces the link of `first`.
      - _Today's runtime, not copied: choosing a second item writes into the
        first._ It makes the cell of every handle one link past its position,
        after the write redirects (`validateAndTransform`), so a handler given a
        state cell that holds a link to an item is given the item, and
        `selected.set(second)` writes a link to the second item into the first
        item's document.
      - _Soundness of values, fixed: `resolveAsCell()` followed no link_, and a
        value `get()` gave carried the address at the end of all links.
      - _A stored link that names no entity, a link within its own document, was
        decoded to the document `""`_ (`#decode` of the adapter), so a read
        through `holder.selected` to `holder.items[0]` gave `undefined`.
      - _A result held a state cell as a plain link with no schema_; a write of
        a compiled piece into a document that no place of it declares and that
        has none yet was dropped (ruling Z3 leaves such a state cell without a
        document); an owner did not take another writer's first write of its
        state cell; and a schema the storage holds by reference (`cid:`) reached
        the executor unresolved, so a reader got no default.
      - _Soundness of labels, fixed: places that decided where a write lands
        still followed every link._ With writes no longer following every link,
        `compare/test/stored-labels.test.ts` found values of `set-over-link` and
        `value-identity` that depend on an input and store no clause of it.
        `Instance.detached` decided what a write replaces by following every
        link, so a handler that stored again the record its cell linked to
        stored a copy in the cell. Under the old rule that copy went back into
        the input, and in `value-identity` it overwrote one element with
        another's values. `#declaredWrite` named the position a write policy is
        checked at the same way. And the result held an input it passes on as a
        plain link: in `writer-policy`, the forger's write through `room.frozen`
        replaced the room's result link, where today's runtime writes the
        protected input and its policy refuses the write.

1061. **What was built (P470).** The result stores a reference to a state cell
      of the instance as a write redirect with the cell's schema, and a
      reference to a position of the argument that it, or a row of it, returns
      as a member or whole as a write redirect (`Instance.stored` with
      `ofResult`); a link inside a member, as a child of a view node, stays
      plain. The adapter keeps the redirect both ways (`#encodeOnce`,
      `#decode`), decodes a link that names no entity to the document it is of,
      resolves a link's schema held by reference, and applies another writer's
      change of a document the executor declared and has not written. A write
      into an absent document no place declares makes it, kind `external`. A
      reference by key whose key no position holds reads as nothing, also where
      a link on the way declares a default (ES §2.5; ruling Z24). ES §4.2 and
      question 86 state the decision.

1062. **What was built (P471).** Where a write lands is one function,
      `Store.landing`: past the write redirects at the position, replacing any
      other link there; a redirect written replaces what the position holds.
      `Store.write`, `Instance.detached` and `#declaredWrite` use it. A handle
      for an input names the cell the instance was given, past the link the
      argument holds to it (`Store.pastBinding`, `Instance.#givenCell` in
      `handleOf`), for a handler and for value code; a link another position
      holds is part of what the cell holds. `get()` and `sample()` give a value
      that carries the position one link past the write redirects
      (`Store.oneLinkPast`, `Handle.#fromPosition`), and a plain value in place
      reached that way stays a copy (ruling Z25). `resolveAsCell()` follows
      every link and reads the positions that hold them and no member.
      `Instance.writeThrough`, a write of a member bound both ways, passes the
      link that binds the attribute. ES §2.4 ("What a handle names, and where
      its reads and writes go") and questions 84 and 85 state it.

1063. **Tests.** `cell-writes.test.ts` has 98 steps on both paths: a handler
      writing through a holder of write redirects, through the chain, and
      through the state cells `Owner` returns, from either path to either path;
      and a handler storing `selected.get()`, `selected.resolveAsCell()` and
      `selected` itself, for a holder's position that holds a link to an item
      document, one that holds a link to an item in place in the holder's list,
      `Selector`'s state cell, an item document passed whole, and a state cell
      `Owner` returns. Where P471 differs from today's path each path has its
      own case:

      | case                                                   | today's path                       | compiled                             |
      | ------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------- | ------------------------------------ |
      | `get()` through a holder's link to a document          | the holder's position              | the item                             |
      | `get()` through a holder's link to an element in place | the holder's position              | a copy                               |
      | `resolveAsCell()` to an element in place               | a copy (a snapshot)                | the element's position               |
      | `Selector` stores `selected` itself                    | the item                           | the state cell                       |
      | `Selector` chooses a second item                       | a link written into the first item | the first item as it was             |
      | `Reader` returns `{ current: selected.get() }`         | the item                           | the input's position in the argument |

      The last one is the crate's: it emits a read that value code returns as
      the input itself. The owner judged it right for value code, which is
      evaluated again when what the position leads to changes. In
      `exec/test/executor.test.ts`, `set-over-link`'s plain value written to a
      cell that holds a link replaces the link, and "keeps the link when the
      same record is stored again" was seen failing first. The comparison of
      values of `set-over-link` stops before `replace`. Three assertions of
      `value-code.test.ts` read the cell's default, `""`, through the redirect.

1064. **Gates.** `exec/test/` 135 files and `compare/test/` 80 files pass;
      `runtime/runner/test/compiled/` 59 files pass; `deno task check`,
      `deno task check-docs`, `deno fmt --check` and `deno lint` pass.

1065. **Not covered.** `get()` of a handle whose declared type is a cell of a
      cell, `Writable<Writable<T>>`, gives a value and not a handle. `push`

1066. **A reference that names nothing reads its default** (replaces the
      sentence of note 1061 on a reference by key that no position holds). The
      owner's decision of 2026-11-24: a read through a reference by key that no
      position holds gives what a read of a place that holds nothing gives, the
      default declared for it, and nothing where none is declared. How long ago

      `Store.locate` takes the default of a declared place, as a state cell, at

      `plan-and-label-templates.md` §1.3, the README, the language subset and

note says `map` or `filter`, it names the case. Times are on an Apple M5 Max
with 18 cores at the load averages given, from other sessions; the counts do not
depend on the load.

1067. **Findings, first.**

        conversation holds an error state in place of its reactions._ The row's
        `tallies.map(...)` is a `map` over a value of the scope `user`; with the

        `Instance.#scopedRows` refuses with the error state "a collection of a
        scope narrower than the space, in a row of another collection". The
        dumps hold 103, 503 and 1,003 of them at 100, 500 and 1,000 messages at

        or figure reported them, and the harness now counts them (`errors` in
        the step `read`). Not fixed; the plan, a place per row and scope key for

        whose inputs read another array of the same document through `*`._ A

1068. **The bisect, and what a send gave per message held.**

      - _Which work_ (profiles at 200 messages, three timed sends each,

1069. **What was built: the records a change of labels reaches (provisional
      decision P472).**
      - _What was asked._ `#recordsReading` collected every set of positions
        registered at, above or below a changed path, and `labelsChanged` then
        asked each set (`#readsChangedLabel`) whether any of its positions in
        the changed document consumes another label in some class, counting one
        whose path names every element as changed. A position unrelated to the
        changed paths was asked about, and the work was every set that read an
        ancestor of a changed path: every row's, in FabriChat, where every row's
        set holds `messages`.
      - _What was built._ The test is made in the walk over the readers of
        labels (`#recordsReading`): each position at, above or below a changed
        path that some record read is asked once whether a read of it consumes
        another label in some class (`OBSERVED_CLASSES`,
        `LabelChange.unchanged`), and only then are its readers taken. A
        position whose path names every element, and every position where the
        store cannot tell, counts as changed, as before. A position of the
        document that no changed path reaches is not asked about: what a read of
        a path consumes is formed from the entries at, above and below it
        (`consumedEntriesForRead`), so a change elsewhere leaves it.
        `#readsChangedLabel` is gone. `Counts.labelReaders` counts the sets
        found.
      - _P472._ As above. It is the rule `LabelChange.unchanged` and
        `plan-and-label-templates.md` §4.1 state ("A label that changes alone":
        a demanded output whose template reaches a slot whose label changed is
        instantiated again); the records it leaves out are those whose positions
        consume the labels they consumed before. Today's runtime keeps no index
        of the records that read a label; this index exists for the compiled
        path (P463), and the walk now costs the positions on the changed paths
        and the readers of those whose label changed.

1070. **What was built: a handler's read of which children a container holds
      (provisional decision P473).**
      - _What was read._ A `shape` or `enumeration` entry of a handler's state
        that gives way to a handle at or above its path places nothing in the
        state; the read made for it (`Host.v` under the schema
        `CHILDREN_UNREAD`, `{ items: {} }`) only had to report the position for
        the slot's binding. That schema types the elements of an array as
        `unknown` and declares no member of a record, so `Store.#copy` copied
        every record and array in place below the position and reported each
        link in it read (as a position that stops). In FabriChat the room's
        result holds the rows of the main conversation in place in the
        executor's store (their storage is in row documents), so the read of
        `self` copied every row.
      - _What was built._ `Host.readChildren` locates the position, following
        the links on the way and at it, and reports it read; nothing below is
        copied or read. A non-reference value is read as before (`v`, under

## Round twenty-six: the rows' reactions, the labels of a body that iterates `get()`, and the rulings Z96 and Z97

Round twenty-six (2026-11-25), on the branch
`claude/compiled-pattern-scoped-rows` from `8442957f6f`. The notes are numbered
from 1077, the provisional decisions from P474. The logs are in the folder
`r26-reactions-rulings/` of the session. Whenever a note says `map` or `filter`,
it names the case. Times are on an Apple M5 Max with 18 cores at the load
averages given, from other sessions; the counts do not depend on the load.

1077. **Findings, first.**
      - _Correctness, fixed: every message row's reactions were an error state._
        A collection of a scope key below a row of another collection, as each
        FabriChat message row's `tallies.map(...)` (a `map` over the result of a
        `computed` of the scope `user`) below the rows of the main conversation,
        was stored as the error state "a collection of a scope narrower than the
        space, in a row of another collection". Its rows are now stored per row
        and scope key (P474, note 1078); the FabriChat dumps hold no error state
        at 100, 500 and 1,000 messages, where they held 103, 503 and 1,003.
      - _Scaling, fixed: a derivation for one principal after another acted
        formed every scoped assembly again._ The assembly of a collection of a
        scope key was not set aside with its element table, so each change of
        the acting key formed it again and marked what used it. With a
        collection of a scope key in each row that is two evaluations per row at
        every change of principal: 20 at 10 rows, 200 at 100. The assembly is
        now set aside with its table (P475, note 1078): 0.
      - _Scaling, open: the places of the inner rows are compared at every
        derivation._ The elements of a `map` over the result of a `computed` are
        read through references by key into the document of that output, which
        no write announces (ruling Z53), so every entry that uses the assembly
        is compared on every pull: one comparison per row and acting key per
        derivation, with no evaluation (10 pulls at 10 rows, 100 at 100;
        `Counts.scopedPulls`). In FabriChat that is one pull per message held at
        each send (note 1083).
      - _Liveness, fixed: the marker of a row's stream was refused at every
        derivation while an element carried a confidentiality clause_ (note
        1027). By Z96 the marker carries the membership label of its row, and
        its document is a store the instance owns (P476, P477, note 1080).
        `apps/redactor/vault.tsx` handles 4 of 4 events with no refusal in each
        of the four modes, where it handled 3 of 4 with 8 refusals, a whole
        resume was refused, and the serving loop with a resume woke no piece;
        `examples/fair-share/main.tsx` gives no refusal where it gave 10, and
        its resume goes through; `system/profile-embed/profile-embed.tsx`
        handles 5 of 5 events where it handled 1 of 5 (note 1084).
      - _Liveness, open, found by step 2: a start whose first derivation reads a
        value under a clause is refused._ The start of a compiled piece runs its
        first derivation in the start's own transaction, which also writes a
        document under no record of the plan (not the result, not in the
        executor's store; not identified further). That document takes the join
        of the transaction and is refused for writer fit (note 1079). Today's
        path runs each node in a transaction of its own and commits.
      - _Soundness, checked (step 2): a body that iterates `items.get()` and
        reads `item.title` stores the items' clauses on the compiled path as on
        today's_, in six layouts on both paths (note 1079). The observation of
        note 1067 holds in the harness of `followed-rows-labels.test.ts` alone,
        not traced.
      - _Structure, found and not fixed: the crate gives no value function to a
        `computed` of a pattern compiled into an element body whose result is
        the source of a collection._ `items.map((item) => Row({ item }))` with
        `Row` declaring `const marks = computed(...)` and returning
        `marks.map(...)` emits the `const` as a local of the setup and no
        `$rt.value`, and the executor fails with "an output that no value
        function computes" (note 1082).
      - _Z97 built: a spread of a record a body builds is a pass_ (note 1081).
        The room's result document holds 110.5 KB where it held 183 KB at 100
        messages.
      - _Scaling, found in this round's own code by the profiles and fixed:_ the
        search for the stream of a new marker walked the whole array of rows a
        splice wrote into (70 ms per FabriChat send at 1,000 messages), and once
        the reactions' rows, which read their position, were evaluated, every
        collection named each element a change moved, since the test was whether
        any collection had a reader of positions (40 ms per send at 1,000). Both
        now follow what changed (note 1083).
      - _Not reproduced: a Topics create of 205 to 206 records with a first
        create refused once_ (note 1074). Four commits from `5fc3cf732c` to the

      - _Traced, not a defect: `system/fabrichat/message-row.tsx` handles 2
