1078. **The rows of a collection of a scope key in a row of another collection
      (step 1; provisional decisions P474 and P475).**
      - _What was stored._ `Instance.#scopedRows` stores the rows of an assembly
        of a scope key whole in the scope instance of the document of the scoped
        outputs, at the path of the result where the collection stands. Below a
        row of another collection the collection has no path of the result, and
        the form was an error state. FabriChat's message row holds
        `tallies.map(...)`, a `map` over the result of a `computed` that reads
        `myProfile`, of the scope `user`; while the rows of the main
        conversation were of that scope the inner collection stood in a row of
        that scope, and the link-following work made the rows of the space (note
        1075).
      - _P474: a place per row and scope key, as P455 has for a value._ Below a
        row of another collection the rows are stored whole in a document of
        their own for the collection and the element keys around it
        (`#rowsDocument`,
        `#identifier("scoped rows", within, keys, { collection })`), with a
        scope instance for each key that evaluated them, and the outer row holds
        a link of that scope to it. The entry that stores them (`#rowsPlace`,
        named `scoped ["rows", collection, ...keys]`) is kept under the outer
        element keys, so it is dropped with them, is set aside per scope key and
        pulled where its inputs changed for the acting key (P456), and is marked
        alone by the restore of a refused commit (`restore`, `#scopedRowsOf`).
        The writes of the document have the records of the output that holds the
        collection, at the array, under the outer keys, and of each output of
        the collection's body at its position in a row, under the outer keys and
        the row's own (`#rowsWrites`); a position below those, such as the rows
        of a collection inside an inner row (`tally.reactors.map` in FabriChat),
        has the record of the nearest of them above it. The same code covers an
        outer `map` over an array of references, over an array of plain values
        in place, and over the result of another per-element construct. Chosen
        as P455's form for a value, a document per row and key; today's runtime
        keeps the result of a row's node in a cell of its own for the row.
      - _P475: the assembly of a collection of a scope key is set aside with its
        element table._ `#forActing` set every entry of another key aside but an
        assembly, whose element table stands beside the entry: the assembly was
        dropped and formed again for each key, and what used it was marked for
        the other key (P458's fourth part). With a collection of a scope key in
        each row, each change of the acting principal formed every row's inner
        assembly again and evaluated every row's place. The table is now set
        aside with the entry (`#asideTables`) and brought back with it; the slot
        stays registered, so a change marks it while it is set aside, as for any
        other entry. This holds for an assembly at a path of the result as well.
      - _Tests_ (`exec/test/scoped-view.test.ts` over
        `fixtures/scoped-nested-rows.tsx`, `-plain` and `-filter`: a `map` over
        an array of references, over an array of plain values in place and over
        the result of a `filter` over an array of references, each row holding a
        `map` over marks of the scope `user`, a `computed` with a block body
        that is not promoted; two principals at 10 and 100 rows): each principal
        reads its own inner rows and no error state is stored; one place per row
        and principal, of a size that does not follow the rows; an edit of one
        item writes that row's place once per principal and the same documents
        at both sizes; a principal's nickname writes its own places alone; a
        refused commit of a place stores that place again and evaluates 1 entry;
        a derivation for a principal after another acted evaluates nothing.
        Before: the error state, 0 places where 90 more at 100 rows, 1 scoped
        write where 2; with P474 and without P475, 20 entries evaluated after

      - _What the pulls cost_ (finding of note 1077): the elements of the inner
        `map` are read through references by key into the document of the

1079. **A body that iterates `items.get()` (step 2).**
      - _The comparison._ `compare/both-paths.ts` compares, for a scenario that
        sets `labels`, the confidentiality clauses stored at and below each

        an array of references once through the elements `items.get()` gives

        start reads no title. Its type of an item declares no clause; each item

        (`labeled-item.tsx`) or a copy in place (`labeled-item-copy.tsx`); the
        reader's type declaring the clause or not; an item type that declares a
        handle among its members, so a read gives each element as a record of
        reads by position; the array given directly or as the `items` of a list
        piece, behind a link (`labeled-list.tsx`). In every layout both paths
        store `item-title` at both outputs after `show`, and the values are
        equal. Two are kept as scenarios of the test (`fixtures/get-iterated`
        and `... through a
        list`), whose only differences are the `flow`
        atoms of a known class.
      - _What today's path does._ The `computed` is a node whose action reads
        through the argument's links into each item document and logs each read;
        the label of the output joins what was read. Where the reader's own type
        declared the clause, today's path stored it at the outputs also before
        `show`, when the body had read no title (the declared clause of the
        argument schema), and the compiled path did not.
      - _The observation of note 1067_ is reproduced only in its own harness:

        titles are made in both (logged from `Store.read`); what the record's
        slot `items/*/title` resolves to in that harness was not traced. Not

1080. **The marker of a row's stream (step 3; ruling Z96; provisional decisions
      P476 and P477).**
      - _The reproduction._ `fixtures/labeled-rows.tsx`: a `map` over an array
        of plain values in place whose elements' names declare the clause
        `person`, each row with a stream and reading its name and `badge`, an
        input of another clause; the handler `add` copies `secret`, stored under
        `person`, into a new element, as fair-share's `joinWithProfile` copies
        the profile's name. Each derivation that made a row wrote the row's
        marker under no record, so the marker took the join (`person` and
        `badge`) and, as a document no schema declares a policy on, was refused
        for writer fit, at every derivation after the first.
      - _P477, Z96's label._ The marker of a stream with element keys has the
        record that the change writing it gave the array that holds the row
        (`membersChanged`, `membersAppended`), with the marker's document as
        target (`RuntimeTransactions.#recordsOfMarkers`, the stream's path in
        the written value found by `streamPaths`). That is the membership of the
        collection, which `plan-and-label-templates.md` §2.6 gives the row of
        the stream index: a stream of an element body exists while the
        collection has the element. The records are taken from what the change
        was given before the array's own record is set apart (`memberships`). A
        marker of a binding with no element step, or of a row whose array the
        change gave no record, keeps the join.
      - _P476: the marker's document is a store the instance owns_ (`#enroll` in
        `#streamEntity`), as the runner enrolls the cell of each stream of a
        piece among its derived internal cells (`pieceOwnedStores`). Without it
        the membership label still misfits: in the fixture, and in fair-share,
        the handler that added the element read the clause, so the membership
        carries it.
      - _Test_ (`runtime/runner/test/compiled/stream-marker-label.test.ts`):
        three adds, no refusal, three rows, and each marker holds `person` and
        not `badge`. Before: a refusal at each derivation after the first; with
        P476 alone, each marker holds `person` and `badge`.
      - _The corpus, each module alone in the four modes_ (before: the run of
        note 1074). `apps/redactor/vault.tsx`: runner 4 of 4, no refusal, equal
        (3 of 4, 8 refusals); after a resume, resumed and 4 of 4 with no refusal
        (the whole resume refused); serving 4 of 4, no refusal, equal (3 of 4,
        8); serving with a resume 4 of 4, no refusal, equal (2 of 4, 4 refusals,
        "the piece did not wake"). `examples/fair-share/main.tsx`: runner 5 of 6
        with no refusal (5 of 6 with 10); after a resume, resumed and 5 of 6
        with no refusal (the whole resume refused); under the serving loop,
        skipped for its `wish`, before and after. Its one event left, "no stream
        of the binding is stored", and its difference from the executor in
        memory (`$value` of a select, "Ada Lovelace" against `myName-text`) are
        those of before, not traced.
      - _Classification_ (`docs/development/cfc-spec-correspondence.md`). The
        label: a conforming implementation. The existence of an element is the
        membership dimension of a collection's structural confidentiality (CFC
        §8.5.6.1, "Member Confidentiality vs Structural Confidentiality": "Child
        paths like `/items/0` carry `shape` (membership/domain)"), and the
        record that gives it is a plan template applied as every compiled record
        is, as a trusted flow-precision claim (§8.9.1). The enrollment: a host
        arrangement, which stores are runtime-owned, under the existing recorded
        gap of derived admission for runtime-owned stores (specs#78; conformance
        statement §5), as today's runner enrolls a stream's cell. No change of
        the specification is needed. Not verified against specs `main` beyond
        the sections quoted.

        tier is one whose members the literal declares. Chosen over the declared
        type of the argument, which the crate does not carry to the emitter.

        `a_spread_of_a_record_the_body_builds_is_a_pass`, seen failing with

        declared path of a spread is that of `a.p`

### CFC questions deferred, round twenty-six

Noted and not resolved, by the owner's instruction of 2026-11-22.

1. P474: the outer row's position that holds the link to the document of the
   inner rows has the template of the output that holds the collection, the
   membership of the inner collection, resolved with the inputs of the run that
   stored the row, which is the run of one scope key; where the inner
   collection's membership label differs between keys, the row of the space
   joins that key's label (question 2 of round twenty-one, for a collection). An
   over-label of the row.
2. P474: a position of an inner row below the outputs of the collection's body,
   such as a row of a collection inside an inner row, has the record of the
   nearest output above it in that row, where the result gives such a position
   the record of the deeper collection's own outputs.
3. P475: no rule of a label changes; an assembly set aside keeps the labels its
   records gave, and a change marks it while it is set aside as it marks any
   entry set aside (question 5 of round twenty-one).
4. Z96 as built (P477): the membership record is the one the change that wrote
   the marker gave the array; a marker written by a change that gave the array
   no record keeps the join of the transaction, an over-label. A marker is
   written once, when its stream is first stored, so a later change of the
   membership label does not reach it.
5. P476: the marker's document is admitted as a store the instance owns, so
   writer fit no longer measures it against an empty ceiling. A marker of a
   binding with no element step now stores the join of the transaction where it
   was refused before (FabriChat round two, question 4): what was a refusal is
   an over-label.
6. Z97 (P478): the members a spread gives are placed with their own labels; the
   record of the whole object is no longer joined into them. A change that
   stores less label, ruled.
7. Note 1079: in the harness of `followed-rows-labels.test.ts`, the output
   `count` of a body that iterates `items.get()` stores the list's clause alone,
   and the look-up of each row its own item's clause alone, where the runtime's
   compiled piece stores every item's clause at the output of such a body. Which
   of the two the template's slot `items/*/title` gives in the harness was not
   traced; `count` itself depends on the enumeration alone.

## Round twenty-seven: a compiled piece created from the CLI and served by a local toolshed

Round twenty-seven (2026-11-25), on the branch
`claude/compiled-pattern-scoped-rows` from `a184f568a0`. The notes are numbered
from 1087, the provisional decisions from P479. The logs are in the folder
`r27-local-e2e/` of the session. No browser was launched. The servers ran at the
port offset 300 (toolshed 8300, shell 5473) with
`EXPERIMENTAL_COMPILED_PATTERNS=true` and the serving loop in Workers, its
default over a file store. Times are on an Apple M5 Max at load averages of 1.8
to 2.5, from other sessions. Whenever a note says `map`, it names the case.

1087. **Findings, first.**
      - _Works end to end:_ `start-local-dev.sh` with the option on starts a
        toolshed whose serving workers compile and serve compiled pieces, and
        `cf piece new` creates the counter
        (`patterns/examples/counter/counter.tsx`), the list fixture
        (`compare/fixtures/serving-list.tsx`) and the FabriChat room copy
        (`compare/fabrichat/fabrichat/room.tsx`) on the compiled path. The
        counter's handlers commit through `cf piece call`, `cf cell get` reads
        it, `cf cell set --input` writes its argument and the piece derives from
        the write, and `cf piece ls` and `cf piece inspect` list it. Following
        every link from each result, a client reads no error state: 0 of 5
        documents (counter), 0 of 605 (list at 300 items), 0 of 247 (room), and
        0 of 83 for Topics on the standard path.
      - _Fixed, the first compiled piece of a fresh space did not start:_ 5 of 7
        `cf piece new` runs in spaces just created waited out the 60-second
        start deadline, and the result document still held nothing minutes
        later. `setUpCompiledPiece` wrote the result's `argument` metadata
        through the result cell, which starts a load of the result document
        while the setup transaction is open; that subscription reached the
        serving loop before the commit, and the loop never started the piece
        once the commit landed. Written through the transaction, 8 of 8 started
        within about a second. The serving loop's part is not fixed: a root
        demanded before the documents that name its compiled source exist is not
        started when they arrive, under the toolshed's serving workers. The
        in-process serving harness does not reproduce it (a client that watches

1088. **The local servers (step 1; P481).** The serving loop runs in Workers by
      default over a file store, and its runtimes had no compiler. The choice
      (P481) is both halves: the toolshed gives the Worker loop a compiler, and
      the script configures the binary. `serveFromPort()` takes `setUpRuntimes`,
      which decides once from the init's experimental options what each serving
      runtime of the worker is given before it serves, and the toolshed's worker
      entry (`runtime/toolshed/lib/serving-worker.ts`) gives it
      `compiledPatternsForServing()` over the worker's own environment, one
      `PatternCompiler` per worker. The process checks the binary at startup
      before any worker starts, as before. So a toolshed serves compiled pieces
      in its default posture, and in whichever posture a deployment picks, which
      a script that set `SERVER_EXECUTION_WORKER=false` would not have given.
      Where the option is on and `PATTERN_COMPILER_BINARY` is unset,
      `start-local-dev.sh` runs `cargo build --release` in
      `base/pattern-compiler` (0.1 s once current) and sets the variable to the
      release binary, so the toolshed compiles with the crate the checkout
      holds, and sets `PATTERN_COMPILER_CACHE_DIR` under the toolshed's
      disposable cache, which workers then share on disk; the restart script
      passes the environment on. The shell takes the option from `/api/meta`,
      which published `compiledPatterns: true`. Test
      `serving-worker-main.test.ts` ("gives each serving runtime it creates what
      the entry decides from the init's experimental options"): before, the verb
      ran with no runtime set up (`receipt` 0 where 1). Its other cases now
      serve over a file store, which a serving worker's runtimes need. A
      toolshed started before a change to `runtime/runner/deno.jsonc` keeps the
      import map it started with while its workers load the new sources, so its
      spare workers failed to start (`Unknown export './compiled/setup'`) until
      it was restarted.

1089. **`cf piece new` (step 2; P479).** Against a deployment that runs the
      serving loop with the option on, as the CLI adopts it from `/api/meta`
      unless its environment sets it, `newPieceWithReceipt` compiles the program
      with the crate's binary at hand first (`checkCompiledProgram`:
      `PATTERN_COMPILER_BINARY`, else the checkout's release build) and decides
      as `Runtime.run` decides under `runCompiledPatterns()`: refused where the
      crate refuses it or a plan requests an effect no built-in answers for a
      compiled piece (`unansweredRequestOf`, moved to `compiled/wish.ts` to be
      shared), accepted otherwise. Accepted, `createCompiledPiece` sets the
      piece up from the client with `compiledInstantiatePiece` (the setup, the
      slug and a creation receipt in the record the served creation keeps, whose
      pattern names the source document), waits within the creation's start
      deadline until the result document holds a value or the serving runtime
      stored why it refused (`compiledPieceStarted`, whose subscription is the
      demand), and then registers the piece through the root with
      `completeServedRegistration`. Refused, the piece is created on the
      standard path. The command prints `Created on the compiled path.` or
      `Created on the standard path:` with the reason, and `--json` names `path`
      and `pathNote`. P479 chose to compile here first because the choice is
      then made before anything is written, by the rule `Runtime.run` applies,
      and a refused program leaves no set-up documents behind; the alternatives
      were to fail on the serving runtime's refusal, or to fall back after it,
      which would have to undo a setup and a creation receipt under the same
      request key. Where no binary is at hand the compiled path is taken
      unchecked, and a refusal by the serving runtime then fails the command
      with the compiler's reason (seen: `$h` is not a listed standard-library
      global), leaving the piece set up and unregistered. A request key replays
      a compiled creation by its receipt, as a served one. Tests, each seen
      failing first: `new-piece-compiled.test.ts` (the module did not export the
      functions), `compiled-instantiate.test.ts` (no export
      `compiledInstantiatePiece`), `compiled-serving.test.ts` "names the
      argument document in the metadata of the result document…" (the link was
      `undefined`) and "is opened by a client of a deployment that serves
      compiled pieces…" (`Cannot start: no pattern identity`). In
      `new-piece-compiled.test.ts`, a refusal that is handled only after the
      write that causes it is awaited crashed the test runner with
      `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading '_idleNext')` in
      `runImmediates`; the test handles it from the start.

### CFC questions deferred, round twenty-seven

Noted and not resolved, by the owner's instruction of 2026-11-22.

1. Note 1093: writing the plan's result schema as the `schema` metadata of a
   compiled piece's result document hands readers the schema's `ifc`
   annotations, from which a client's label view derives labels
   (`cfcLabelViewFromSchema`). Whether a reader may take a compiled piece's
   labels from that schema, which the store does not verify against the template
   labels, is open.
2. `setUpCompiledPiece` writes the `argument` link into the result document's
   metadata from the client's setup transaction, with
   `rawMetaWriteAuthorization`, as the runner's setup does; the label that
   commit stores at the metadata path is the client transaction's join, and
   whether a template label of the plan ever covers that path was not traced.
3. P480 changes no rule of a label: the one list document is written under the
   label each chunk was written under. A reader of the list now reads one
   document where it read several, and so joins one label.

1099. **Removing a row from its own button (step 3; P482).** Reproduced with
      `patterns/examples/todo-list` itself on the executor and on the runner
      (scratch scripts): on the executor the row's button removed the item, over
      an array of references and over an array of plain values in place, because
      the event stayed in the executor's queue; on the runner the event arrived
      (5 events handled for 3 adds and one click) and the list's action was
      handed `{}` with no address, while the list held three links to row
      documents. P482: an event that a body sends is stored as what a body
      writes is (ES §2.4): `Instance.queue` stores `returned` of the event, so a
      handle, a reference stand-in and a container that carries its address are
      each a link, in the executor's queue and in what a compiled piece sends
      on. And a handler is handed its event as its slots of root `event` read it
      (`Instance.#handedEvent`): a link at a position the body reads through is
      the value read through it, carrying its address (`HandedValues.note`); a
      link the body reads by `identity` alone is given by `handleOf` (a
      reference stand-in where the event declares data, a handle where it
      declares a cell; `handleOf` now makes the stand-in for a slot of root
      `event` as for one of root `binding`). A slot that reads through such a
      link is bound to the event's position and to the positions the read
      crossed. ES §2.4 ("An event a body sends, and the links an event holds")
      states it. The alternative, keeping the stand-in's address in what the
      piece sends, would have left an event from outside unmatched and a member
      read through it `undefined`.

## Round twenty-nine: the board's Start button, a topic's own verbs, and the FabriChat send

Round twenty-nine (2026-11-25), on the branch
`claude/compiled-pattern-scoped-rows` from `9b0d83a3d0`. The notes are numbered
from 1110, the provisional decisions from P485. The logs are in the folder
`r29-topics-start-verbs/` of the session. No browser was launched. The round's
own toolshed ran at port 8400 with its store in the session's scratch folder.
Three requests of the coordinator came during the round and went first: the
FabriChat send refused after `9b0d83a3d0`, the empty message window after a
restart, and the cost of a Topics create that grows with the board. Whenever a
note says `map`, it names the case.

1110. **Findings, first.**
      - _Scaling, open: every new session derives every topic of the board._
        A Topics create from the CLI, where each `cf` call is a session of its
        own, changes about 132 + 5.4n documents and 165 KB + 39 KB·n at n
        topics held (`create-cost.sh` of the session's scratch folder, 1 to 40
        topics, the compiled board on the round's toolshed). Of a create at 40
        topics, 242 documents (1.04 MB) are of the scope `session` of the
        creating call: each topic's view reads state of that scope, so its
        outputs are stored per session, and the serving loop derives every
        topic for every session that demands the board, about 6 documents and
        25 KB per topic and new session. Each earlier session also stores the
        board's scoped outputs again at each change (6 documents, 26 KB each,
        for three earlier sessions). A browser session pays the same once, at
        its first load. This is the open item "a session no client holds any
        more is still derived at every change" together with derivation by
        demand, which neither exists on the compiled path; today's path
        derives a session's instance of a topic only where something of that
        session demands it. Not fixed (note 1116).
      - _Soundness, fixed (P489): the first append onto a list of the
        argument that the storage did not hold stored a record._ The first
        message of a FabriChat room wrote `{ 0: <link>, length: 1 }` at the
        argument's `messages`, since the adapter wrote the number of members
        and the position added onto an absent array. The executor kept its
        own array, so nothing showed until a serving runtime took the space
        over and read the list from the storage: it found no array, and the
        next send stored a list of one. A room created before this fix keeps
        the record (no migration, by the owner's word on compatibility).
      - _CFC, the owner's ruling Z99 and its refinement, built (note 1112):_
        a stream's entries document is measured under no join, and of the
        transaction's join only an entry's `payload`, `error` and `reason`
        keep a stamp. The consumer of an event is handed the payload as a
        value and consumes no label of it, as before (top/3175). With the
        residency refusal gone, a served handler that read another space's
        labeled value can now send it on in an event, and the handler of that
        event writes it unlabeled: the under-taint now reaches across spaces.
        Said first because it stores and enforces less.
      - _Not working end to end on the compiled path, the board's crossrefs:_
        after `mention` commits, the board's `crossrefs` list no source for
        the mentioned topic, where today's path lists two. The topic's stored
        `mentioned` holds the link, but its `mentions` output, which the lift
        `mentionsOf` returns from `mentioned: unknown[]`, holds a copy of each
        mentioned topic's result, which no topic of the board equals. A
        function body reads a value reached through a link as a copy with no
        address, so returning it unchanged stores the copy, against ES §2.4;
        reproduced on the executor with a `lift` that returns the elements of
        an array of references it declares `unknown[]` (stored
        `[{"title":"a"},{"title":"b"}]` where today's path stores the links).
        Not fixed (note 1118).
      - _Not working on the compiled path, `cf cell set <topic> title`:_
        refused with `updated result does not match its write destination:
        missing required property comments`. The CLI validates the whole
        argument document against the argument schema, and a topic's argument
        document lacks the defaults its type declares: the compiled path
        writes those only where the type declares a write policy
        (`argumentWithDefaults`), and today's setup writes them all.
      - _Not built, step 4 (note 1115)._

1111. **The Start button (step 1).** The handler `submitProfileTopic` read the
      draft `newTitle` blank. The executor names the state cell of the scope
      `session` by one name for every key, and `RuntimeTransactions.load`
      treated every document whose name is no entity of its own (`of:`) as one
      the executor makes, so the instance of a session key the executor held
      no copy of was never read from the replica and the executor gave the
      declared default. The coordinator's guess, another session's instance,
      did not hold: the handler ran stamped with the client's session. A
      document of a scope is now read from the replica for a key the executor
      holds no copy of (P490); a resumed instance reads it as before. And
      where the piece had read such an instance as absent, the client's later
      write of it was dropped: the subscription asked whether the place was
      declared by the name of the instance, where the executor declares a
      place of a scope by its one name. Test
      `runtime/runner/test/compiled/session-draft.test.ts` over
      `compare/fixtures/session-draft.tsx`, three cases under the serving
      loop, each seen failing first (`8b701ee867`). The board's `profileName`,
      a value of the scope `user` the handler is bound to, is the second case

1112. **The FabriChat send (the coordinator's first request).** The send
      handler, which reads the sender's profile from the profile's own space,
      appends `{ messageAct: true }` to the event log of the room's
      `tellJoined` stream in its own transaction. The preparation measured the
      append against the log's empty ceiling where the join came from another
      space (`isDeclarablePolicyStore` skips a stream's entries document only
      for a local join), and refused it at `/entries`. Today's path prepares
      the same append the same way; P482 did not change the label. The owner
      ruled (Z99) that the sidecar is internal state of the event queue, which
      needs no labels, with the refinement that events themselves may carry
      labels and are to keep them. Built: no write to an entries document is
      measured, and of the join only the positions that say what an event or

      same way. Classified as a host arrangement under
      `docs/development/cfc-spec-correspondence.md` (where the queue keeps its
